items.note: Compares 6,875 essays (human-only, AI-only, and three Human+AI prompt strategies) on quality and structural homogenization; search notes say the Human+AI essays are GPT-5-mini rewrites of existing AIDE corpus essays, so no person received AI help (could also be read as model_only).

Uses the ChatGPT release as a natural experiment on about 7,500 master's admissions applications; outcomes are writing quality, AI use, and admission, plus an admissions-officer perception experiment, with no creativity or diversity outcome (borderline: next stage may check whether essay quality counts).

Two preregistered experiments (3,750 participants in total, split not stated) compare prompting and output performance across generative-model versions, including an open-ended creative image task; the comparison is between AI configurations (model upgrade, automated prompt rewriting).

Compares 957 student debates with an AI adversary by modality (voice versus text) on repetition and breadth of ideas; how modality was assigned and the number of students are not stated, so it may be observational.

System paper (HALO) for molecular hypothesis generation with an expert study of 10 medicinal chemists reporting higher-quality, more diverse candidate molecules; the comparison condition is not described in the abstract, and N is below 50.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC empty; ScienceDirect 403); per search notes, a linked Mendeley dataset describes 76 undergraduates in a Doubao-assistant group versus a no-device control on a poster design task with blind novelty ratings, link to this article unverified.

224 students randomly assigned to 97 online triads (human-only, supportive-AI persona, contrarian-AI persona) on an individual-group-individual movie-plot task; creative performance is linked to conditions; journal version of arXiv 2512.18239; next stage should check whether the final individual phase gives an after_ai outcome.

Two-group quasi-experiment in a Chinese vocational college comparing project-based learning in an AI-enabled immersive virtual environment with traditional project-based learning on design and creative ability; whether the agents are generative AI and the sample size are not stated.

Preregistered RCT on creative writing with an interactive AI assistant varying incentives (originality relative to peers versus quality) and measuring collective diversity; search notes report a 2x2 with an AI-versus-alone arm and N = 200, which the abstract does not state.

2,234 participants randomly assigned to human-human or human-AI-agent teams producing 11,024 ads, rated by independent raters and tested on X; human-AI teams produced higher text quality, lower image quality, and more homogeneous outputs (version 3).
